recognize_zh: CD20 染色時，胸腺小葉大部分淋巴球為陰性（藍色），只有左下方一團 B 細胞及少數散在細胞呈棕色膜陽性，說明此淋巴組織以 T 細胞為主、B 細胞僅佔少數。
features: Most lymphocytes within the thymic lobules are CD20-negative
Discrete aggregate of strongly membranous CD20-positive B cells at the lower-left edge of the lobule (medullary/perivascular B-cell zone)
Scattered CD20-positive B cells within the lobule and between thyroid follicles
No expanded or nodular B-cell follicles with germinal centers
Thyroid follicles negative; colloid shows faint nonspecific tan background
describe_en: CD20 immunohistochemistry shows that the majority of lymphoid cells in the thymic lobules are negative, with a discrete cluster of CD20-positive B cells at one edge and scattered positive cells extending between the thyroid follicles. There is no nodular B-cell expansion. The distribution is the reciprocal of the CD3 stain and is consistent with the small normal thymic B-cell population. Findings are consistent with a cervical thymic remnant with intermixed ectopic thyroid tissue.

ddx.dx: Reactive lymph node or lymphocytic thyroiditis
ddx.vs: These show CD20-positive follicles with germinal centers as a major component, whereas here B cells are a minor, localized population within a T-cell-predominant lobule.
Thymic MALT lymphoma shows sheets of CD20-positive B cells with lymphoepithelial lesions and cystic change, not the sparse B cells seen here.
